newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees orders quickly covered.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees orders quickly covered.

text.p: Shipbrokers quickly fixed tonnage for a number of this week's sugar freight orders by Wednesday but most business was routine with no discernible pattern to the demand for origins, they said.
Genoc fixed 14/15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to Morocco with Mediterranean and Black Sea options for September/October dates.
E D & F Man fixed 15,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to Aqaba for mid-October and a further 12,000 tonnes from east coast India to Indonesia/Colombo for early October, they said.
Louis Dreyfus fixed 14,300 tonnes from Santos to the Red Sea for early October dates, market sources said.
Fiji Sugar Marketing was reported to still be on subjects with its Fiji to Japan order, which shipbrokers said was likely to achieve a rate close to $22.
The only new business reported on Wednesday came from Mauritius Sugar Syndicate, which quoted for 14/14,250 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London for 14/18 October.

Elsewhere, Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service said 39 vessels were berthed at south Brazil's key Santos port of which 15 were sugar loaders. Two sugar loaders were also berthed at Rio de Janeiro, it said.
Sugar exports from Brazil's northern port of Recife are already higher than last year for the month of September, according to port's docking manager.
The port has 16 berths available for sugar loading, one of which is a bulk terminal which has a nominal capacity of 1,000 tonnes an hour.
Port officials said Maceio has yet to see any exports of 1996/97 north/northeast sugar.
